messages:
devon: Hey team — hitting a weird one on Android 13 with our Kotlin SDK. Using Retrofit + a suspend CallAdapter, occasionally a single API call results in two POSTs (duplicate side effects). Only reproducible on Pixel 8 emulator and some user devices. Anyone seen this?

kevin: Yep. Saw something similar last week. Is this happening with OkHttp 4.x or 5.x? Any stack traces or okhttp logs?

maria: fwiw, I hit duplicates when our coroutine job got cancelled and then resumed; Retrofit adapter retried the Call object. Could be Call re-execution + lack of idempotency.

devon: Using OkHttp 4.11.0, Retrofit 2.9 with a custom suspend adapter (we use a small CallAdapterFactory to return `suspend fun`). Repro steps: 1) start request, 2) trigger process-level GC + configuration change (rotate orientation) or OS background throttle, 3) request ends up being executed twice. Attached a small log snippet: 
```
I/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.prod.example.com/v1/submit
I/OkHttp: --> END POST (123-byte body)
I/OkHttp: <-- 500 Internal Server Error https://api.prod.example.com/v1/submit (456ms)
I/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.prod.example.com/v1/submit
I/OkHttp: --> END POST (123-byte body)
I/OkHttp: <-- 200 OK https://api.prod.example.com/v1/submit (22ms)
```

sam: Oof. Sounds like the Call object got enqueued twice or `execute()` was called again after a cancel. Are you using `Call.clone()` anywhere? Retrofit's adapter should create a fresh Call per invocation.

kevin: Can you share the adapter code? My gut: when coroutine gets cancelled we might be re-subscribing and accidentally re-creating the request. Also Android 13 introduced stricter foreground/background scheduling which can surface races.

devon: Adapter snippet (simplified):
```
class SuspendCallAdapterFactory: CallAdapter.Factory() {
  override fun get(...): CallAdapter<*, *>? {
    return object: CallAdapter<Any, Any> {
      override fun adapt(call: Call<Any>): Any {
        return suspendCoroutine { cont ->
          call.enqueue(object: Callback<Any> { ... onResponse -> cont.resume(response.body()) ... })
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

maria: Ah — your adapter closes over the original `call` instance. If the coroutine gets cancelled and restarted, the same `call` might be reused. Try creating `val fresh = call.clone()` inside `adapt` and use `fresh.enqueue(...)` so each adapt call has its own lifecycle. Also wire cancellation: `cont.invokeOnCancellation { fresh.cancel() }`.

sam: Adding to that: set a per-call tag for dedupe on the server (short-term mitigation). For crash-proofing on Android, ensure `Dispatchers.IO.limitedParallelism(...)` isn't causing weird dispatcher reuse.

devon: Nice catch — I was assuming Retrofit always gives a fresh Call. Will change to clone. Quick test after cloning: no duplicates in 200 runs on Pixel 8 emulator. Thanks! :raised_hands:

ci-bot: CI run for branch `fix/retrofit-clone-adapter` finished: 24/24 tests passed.

kevin: Great. Can we add a unit test that simulates cancellation + restart? Maybe use a fake OkHttp client that records requests. Also add a small comment in the adapter about cloning to avoid reuse.

maria: I'll open a tiny PR to our sample-app that demonstrates the cancellation repro and the clone fix, plus a short note in the devdocs about adapter pitfalls on Android.

devon: Awesome — will close the ticket after PR lands. Thanks everyone.
